title: Restoring cervical lordosis by cervical extension traction methods (systematic review)
n: 299 treated (315 controls) — 9 controlled trials (6 RCT, 3 nRCT) of 1,001 screened
correction: 12–18° lordosis increase; 6–25 mm reduction in anterior head translation
followUp: Stable to 15.5 months (up to 3.5° / 19% loss at longest follow-up); untreated controls (n=315) showed zero lordosis increase

title: Structural rehabilitation of the cervical lordosis and forward head posture (case reports)
correction: 14.1° mean lordosis improvement (SD 9.7°); 12 mm forward-head-posture reduction
followUp: 38% of cases (n=23) followed ~1.8 years; slight lordosis loss (3.1°) but pain/disability gains maintained

title: Restoring lumbar lordosis (systematic review of controlled trials)
n: 120 treated (102 controls) — 3 trials (2 RCT, 1 nRCT) of 574 screened
painOutcome: Maintained at 6 months (RCTs); comparison groups regressed toward baseline by 3 months
followUp: 6 months (RCTs), maintained; 1.5 years with periodic maintenance care (nRCT); untreated controls (n=102) showed zero increase

title: Structural rehabilitation of the lumbar lordosis (case reports)
followUp: Varies by report; findings consistent with controlled-trial results

title: Reducing thoracic hyperkyphosis subluxation deformity (systematic review)
studyType: Systematic review (4 case reports, 2 case series, 1 RCT)
n: 7 peer-reviewed papers (~17 patients average per included study)
correction: 12° average thoracic curve reduction (vs. 3° in exercise-only comparison trials)
painOutcome: Improved pain, disability, quality-of-life measures; some vital-capacity improvement
followUp: Not consistently reported across included studies

title: CBP methods to reduce lateral head translation posture
n: Trial: treated vs. 26 untreated controls; Case reports: 14 patients
correction: 7 mm reduction (trial); ~18 mm average reduction (case reports) — lateral translation, not degrees
painOutcome: >3-point drop (trial) vs. no change in 26 controls; 4.3-point improvement (case reports)

title: CBP methods to reduce lateral thoracic translation (pseudo-scoliosis) posture
n: Trial: 63 chronic low-back-pain patients vs. 23 controls; Case reports: 6 patients
correction: 8 mm reduction (trial); 23 mm average reduction (case reports) — lateral translation, not degrees
painOutcome: 2-point drop (trial) vs. no change in 23 controls; 4-point drop (case reports)

title: Improving the pediatric cervical lordosis (case reporting review)
correction: 25° lordosis increase; 12.3 mm atlas-plane-line increase; 7.2 mm anterior-head-translation reduction
followUp: 6/11 (55%) reported follow-up, 3 months–15 years; secondary gains reported in headaches, ADHD/concentration, dizziness, enuresis, otitis media
